case_name: Jandel Singh v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

8  May  2003
Appeal (civil) 1690 of 1996
The Judgment was delivered by : Ashok Bhan, J.

facts: Seven persons were named in a First Information Report (FIR) for the murder of Prakash, which took place at Village Kheri.
The FIR was lodged by Ramgopal Chipa, PW1, who was present at the place of occurrence when the incident took place.
A3 died during trial and A6 has not preferred any appeal.
A1 Meharban Singh and A2 Pratap Singh absconded.
Uday Bhan Singh, A4, Nawab Singh, A5, Nirpat Singh, A6 (since deceased) and Jandel Singh, A7 were tried in Criminal Trial No. 54/1980.
They were convicted under Section 120-B, 147, 302 read with Section 149 of IPC.
The appeals were partly accepted by the High Court.
Jandel Singh, A7 has filed Criminal Appeal No. 1690 of 1996 and the other two accused Uday Bhan Singh, A4 and Nawab Singh, A5 have filed Criminal Appeal No. 1691 of 1996 in this Court.
issues: Whether the prosecution's version is improbable?
Whether the testimony of eye witnesses inspires confidence?
Whether the Investigating Officer carried out a proper investigation?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution story is highly improbable.
The intention, if at all, was to kill Prakash(deceased) only.
It is unlikely that the two eye witnesses would also be invited along with the deceased.
respondent_arguments: There is no specific injury which could cause death in the ordinary course of nature had been attributed to any of the appellants.
The main accused with whom the deceased had litigation have already been acquitted in a subsequent trial.
court_reasoning: The story put forth by the prosecution is highly improbable.
The testimony of eye witnesses does not inspire confidence being untrustworthy.
The Investigating Officer did not carry out a proper investigation.
holding: Both the appeals are allowed and the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants is set aside.
Appellants are on bail. Their bail bonds are ordered to be discharged. Appeal allowed.
